title: Integral finite models of a finite etale cover after shrinking
statement:
Let $C$ be an integral Noetherian scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme], where Noetherian means admitting a finite affine open cover by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Let $U\subseteq C$ be a nonempty affine open subscheme [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-affine-spectrum], and let $g:T\to U$ be a finite etale surjective morphism [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-etale-morphism, def-weil-surjective-morphism]. There exist a nonempty affine open $W\subseteq U$, a nonempty finite index set $A$, integral schemes $Y_a$ and finite morphisms $q_a:Y_a\to C$ for $a\in A$, such that $V_a=Y_a\times_CW$ [def-pc-fibre-product] is a nonempty open subscheme of $Y_a$, and there is an isomorphism of $W$-schemes
$$T\times_UW\ \cong\ \coprod_{a\in A}V_a.$$
In particular the whole inverse image of $W$ in $\coprod_aY_a$ is identified with $T\times_UW$, not merely with an open subscheme thereof.

source.place: Tag 05K0, lemma-quasi-finite-separated-pass-through-finite; agent-written refinement by reduced closures of the generic components and shrinking away their intersections

proof.text: Put $i:U\hookrightarrow C$ and $f=i\circ g$. The scheme $C$ is quasi-compact by its finite affine cover and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated]. The open immersion $i$ is quasi-compact because its inverse images in Noetherian affine opens are quasi-compact; this is included in [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian]. Thus $i$ has finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-qc-open-immersion-finite-type]. A finite algebra is generated as an algebra by any finite module generating set, so $g$ has finite type; [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change] gives finite type of $f$. The fibres of $f$ are either fibres of $g$ or empty, hence finite by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-closed-map-finite-fibres]; [pqf-lem-qf-finitefibres] makes $f$ quasi-finite. Finally $g$ is separated by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-closed-map-finite-fibres]. Since $i$ is a monomorphism, $T\times_C T=T\times_U T$ by the pullback universal property, and the diagonal of $f$ is the closed diagonal of $g$. Therefore $f$ is separated.

source.place: Tag 05K0, verification of the finite-type separated quasi-finite hypotheses; Tags 01OY, 01T3 and 02NH

proof.text: Apply [thm-pqf-zmt-factorization] to $f$. Obtain $j:T\hookrightarrow P$ a quasi-compact open immersion and $p:P\to C$ finite with $p\circ j=f$. The open $U$ is integral: its nonempty affine opens are nonempty affine opens of $C$, hence have domain coordinate rings by [def-pc-integral-scheme]. Therefore $U$ is reduced, and [etale-proposition-etale-reduced] makes $T$ reduced. Let $Z\hookrightarrow P$ be the scheme-theoretic image of $j$. By [lem-trf-reduced-scheme-image] it is the reduced induced closed subscheme on $\overline{j(T)}$, and by [lemma-nagata-immersion-open-in-scheme-image] the induced $T\hookrightarrow Z$ is a dense open immersion. The morphism $r:Z\to C$ is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-finite] and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-composition].

In fact $Z\times_C U$ equals $T$ as a $U$-scheme. To check this, put $P_U=p^{-1}(U)$ and let $j_U:T\hookrightarrow P_U$ be the induced open immersion. The map $p_U:P_U\to U$ is finite directly from the affine definition of a finite morphism: over every affine open of $U$, its ring map is the same finite ring map as for $p$. It is separated by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-closed-map-finite-fibres]. Since $p_U\circ j_U=g$ is finite, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-permanence-over-separated] makes $j_U$ finite, hence a closed map. Thus $T$ is closed in $P_U$, and so also in $Z\cap P_U$. But $T$ is dense in $Z$ and contained in this open subset; consequently $Z\cap P_U=T$ topologically. The map $T\hookrightarrow Z\cap P_U$ is an open immersion onto the whole space and hence an isomorphism by [def-weil-open-immersion]. The pullback universal property identifies this open restriction with $Z\times_C U$.

Let $\eta$ be the generic point of $U$, also the generic point of $C$. It exists by [lem-sc-scheme-sober], since $U$ is nonempty and integral. Apply [lem-sbc-finite-etale-generic-fibre-cover-density] with base $S=U$, smooth map $c=\mathrm{id}_U:U\to U$, and the etale map $g:T\to U$. The identity is smooth directly from the lifting definition [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]: it has finite presentation and every prescribed map over $U$ lifts by the structure map. The lemma gives density of $T_\eta\to T$. Its function-field generic fibre is the residue-field fibre [def-pc-scheme-fibre], since on any nonempty affine domain chart the stalk at the zero prime is its field of fractions. The underlying fibre is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-closed-map-finite-fibres], discrete by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-fibre-discrete-separable-points], and identified with $g^{-1}(\eta)$ by [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. It is nonempty by surjectivity of $g$. Write its distinct points as $t_a$ for a nonempty finite index set $A$. Their image is dense in $T$, hence in $Z$.

source.place: Tag 02GL (lemma-etale-over-field), Tag 01UA for the generic-fibre density input

proof.text: For $a\in A$, let $H_a=\overline{\{t_a\}}\subset Z$. It is irreducible by [lem-weil-pbc-irreducible-closure]. Give $H_a$ its reduced induced closed subscheme structure $Y_a\hookrightarrow Z$ using [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. It is nonempty, reduced and irreducible, hence integral by [def-pc-integral-scheme]. The map $q_a:Y_a\to C$ is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-finite] and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-composition]. The finite closed union $\bigcup_a H_a$ contains the dense set $\{t_a:a\in A\}$, so it equals $Z$. Each $H_a$ meets the fibre over $\eta$ in exactly $t_a$: any such point is a specialization of $t_a$, and specialization in the discrete subspace $r^{-1}(\eta)=g^{-1}(\eta)$ forces equality. In particular $H_a\cap H_b$ has no point over $\eta$ when $a\ne b$. This argument proves the needed component property directly; it assumes no normality of $C$ or disjointness of components before shrinking.

source.place: Tag 01J3 (lemma-reduced-closed-subscheme); Topology Tag 004W; finite-union and specialization argument

proof.text: Set $B=\bigcup_{a\ne b}r(H_a\cap H_b)$. Every intersection is closed in $Z$ and $r$ is finite, so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-closed-map-finite-fibres] shows that $B$ is closed in $C$. It avoids $\eta$ by the preceding step. Choose an affine open $W$ with $\eta\in W\subseteq U\setminus B$ using [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]. The open restriction $Z_W=r^{-1}(W)$ is the open $T\times_U W$ by Step 3. The closed subsets $H_a\cap Z_W$ cover it and are pairwise disjoint. Since there are finitely many of them, each is also open, its complement being the union of the others. Each contains $t_a$ and is nonempty.

source.place: Tag 01WN (finite morphisms are closed); Schemes Tag 01IT (lemma-basis-affine-opens)

proof.text: Put $V_a=Y_a\times_C W$. Pullback along an open inclusion is the inverse-image open subscheme: for any scheme mapping to $Y_a$ with image over $W$, the unique map into this open restriction has precisely the pullback universal property [def-pc-fibre-product, def-weil-open-immersion]. Thus $V_a$ is open in $Y_a$ and nonempty because it contains $t_a$. Its closed immersion into $Z_W$ has support $H_a\cap Z_W$. This is a reduced induced closed subscheme: on each affine open it is defined by the same radical ideal as $Y_a\hookrightarrow Z$ restricted to that open, by the affine-local construction in [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. The open subscheme of the reduced scheme $Z_W$ on $H_a\cap Z_W$ is itself reduced and is a closed subscheme, since the support is clopen; on affine charts its local rings are localizations of the reduced ambient coordinate rings. Uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme] identifies this open subscheme with $V_a$. Hence the $V_a$ are disjoint open subschemes covering $Z_W$. Gluing their inclusion maps and the inverse restrictions gives mutually inverse maps $\coprod_a V_a\simeq Z_W\simeq T\times_U W$ over $W$, using the scheme coproduct universal property [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]. The pullback universal property also identifies the inverse image of $W$ in $\coprod_aY_a$ with $\coprod_a V_a$; the comparison is on the entire inverse image.

source.place: Tags 01J3 and 01J4, affine-local reduced induced structure; gluing the finite disjoint open cover

Sources checked: Stacks 05K0 (more-morphisms.tex l.12457) against thm-pqf-zmt-factorization, and 056B (morphisms.tex l.977) against lem-trf-reduced-scheme-image. Step 1 checks every ZMT hypothesis: i is a quasi-compact open immersion because open subsets of Noetherian C are quasi-compact (01OW); C is quasi-separated (01OY); f has finite type and finite fibres, so it is quasi-finite (02NH); f is separated because i is a monomorphism, so T×_C T=T×_U T. Step 3 is correct: j_U is finite by 035D(1), so T is closed, open and dense in Z∩P_U, hence equal to it and r^{-1}(U)=T. Step 4 applies the generic-fibre density lemma with c=id_U and needs no normality. In Steps 5–6 the generic fibre is discrete, so each H_a meets r^{-1}(η) only in t_a, and the finite closed map r removes the pairwise intersections. Step 7 identifies V_a with the clopen open subscheme of Z_W by 01J3(3) uniqueness, so the comparison covers the whole inverse image. The statement is unchanged and the citer lem-per-constructible-finite-open-constant-generation uses it consistently. Edge cases checked: U=C, C the spectrum of a field, components meeting in Z, non-normal C. There are no new nodes and no duplicate (rg for 05K0, integral models, finite étale/integral/shrink; the r1 compactification node is only for curves over k=k̄, and lem-trf-finite-base-splits-etale is a different statement). Batch 5: lem-trf-reduced-scheme-image is the generic Stacks lemma 056B, not part of the trace-formula or Poincaré-duality proofs. Its 20-node closure contains no other sec-trace-formula or sec-poincare-duality node, and the proof does not really need it, so it is accepted. lean.statement: theorem exists_finite_etale_integral_models_after_shrinking (C : Scheme.{u}) [IsIntegral C] [IsNoetherian C] (U : C.Opens) (hU : IsAffineOpen U) (hUne : Nonempty U) {T : Scheme.{u}} (g : T ⟶ U.toScheme) [IsFinite g] [Etale g] [Surjective g] : ∃ W : U.toScheme.Opens, IsAffineOpen W ∧ Nonempty W ∧ ∃ (A : Type u) (_ : Finite A) (_ : Nonempty A) (Y : A → Scheme.{u}) (q : ∀ a : A, Y a ⟶ C), (∀ a : A, IsIntegral (Y a) ∧ IsFinite (q a) ∧ Nonempty ↥(pullback (q a) (W.ι ≫ U.ι)) ∧ IsOpenImmersion (pullback.fst (q a) (W.ι ≫ U.ι))) ∧ ∃ e : pullback g W.ι ≅ ∐ (fun a : A ↦ pullback (q a) (W.ι ≫ U.ι)), e.hom ≫ Sigma.desc (fun a : A ↦ pullback.snd (q a) (W.ι ≫ U.ι)) = pullback.snd g W.ι
